text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad who is on a three-day official visit to Lebanon said: "Malaysia will contribute to the rebuilding process of Lebanon".
- Lebanon's parliamentary foreign affairs committee demanded the cancellation of the Mideast economic summit to be held in Qatar in November which Israel is expected to attend.

- The consolidated balance sheet of Lebanon's commercial banks rose in dollar terms to $25,210 million at the end of April from $24,737 million a month earlier according to the Lebanese Banks Association.
- Lebanon's public debt rose by 2.51 percent in May over April according to figures issued by the Lebanese Banks Association.
- The judicial authorities start interrogating suspects accused of embezzling billions of Lebanese pounds from the port of Beirut authority.
- Syrian Vice-President Khaddam said: "Lebanon is recovering (from the civil war) in very fast steps".
- Georgia released Lebanese businessman Roger Tamraz who is wanted in Lebanon on charges of embezzlement.
- The Lebanese police destroyed a big amount of confiscated drugs.
